summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, chronic hemolytic anemia, and heart failure, was admitted for fever and confusion following an elotuzumab infusion. His symptoms were attributed to an infusion-related reaction, with no evidence of active infection on blood or urine cultures. He was treated with a course of antibiotics as a precaution and monitored closely. His encephalopathy resolved, and he remained afebrile by discharge. He had stable vital signs, improved kidney function, and no active bleeding despite persistent anemia and thrombocytopenia. Aspirin was held due to low platelets, and pomalidomide was paused pending oncology follow-up. He completed dialysis during admission, remained on fidaxomicin for C. difficile colitis, and was discharged to extended care rehab with clear mental status and a plan for close outpatient follow-up.
